⛔ **NO `@reboot` CRON LINE, AND THE ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE FOR TWO SEPARATE REASONS.** Boot is the one moment the verdict IS already consumed, twice — an `@reboot` check would duplicate a guard that exists. And Docker reports `starting` during a healthcheck's `start_period`, which this script counts as NOT healthy: correct for steady state, a **guaranteed false positive at boot**. An alert that cries wolf on every cold start is the noise `OQ-067` rejected. Every 15 minutes instead.
⚠ **NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION** — `DEC-094` d7's precedent, operator-ruled: a refinement beyond a satisfied requirement. No requirement covers *the healthcheck's verdict has a consumer*; `NFR-046`'s four operational alerts do not, which is the exact mis-binding `SC-041` had to correct on `WBS-26.2`. The forced-refusal suite is the evidence, and trap 16c is not strained by a criterion that is never written.

✅✅✅ **VERDICT RECORDED 2026-09-01: `Implemented`, THE OPERATOR'S RULING, AGAINST THE GENERATED SLATE (`scripts/gen-slice-review-slate.mjs SL-035`) AND NOT A SUMMARY (`LL-011`). No waiver, no `force`.** The agent's disclosure at the asking, stated so the verdict is not read as resting on more than it did: all five named artifacts were verified present and wired (`ci.yml:126`, `deploy/scripts/crontab.example:85`, `deploy/runbooks/cloud-operations.md` §5); the forced-refusal suite ran GREEN locally at 10 cases / 13 assertions and on CI run `33464043150`; and the calibration was RE-RUN independently rather than taken from this row — neutering the `emit_to_seq` call site failed **exactly three** assertions, all Seq-family, and the nested `EventType` assertion FAILS through its `else` branch rather than vanishing, so it is fail-closed. ⭐ **The hardest constraint was proven by the DIFF, not by inspection**: `git show --name-only b515fc64` touched **neither compose file**, so `service_healthy` was not restored by construction; the api-dependent site at `deploy/docker-compose.yml:376-377` still reads `condition: service_started` with its `DEF-079` rationale intact. ⚠ **WHAT WAS EXPLICITLY NOT CLAIMED:** the script has never run against a live stack or detected a real unhealthy container — every branch is exercised with `docker` and `curl` stubbed on PATH — and the Seq alert RULE remains unversionable configuration that no test can see.

DW-086 - A LIGHTWEIGHT PER-MEETING AGENDA PROJECTION SO THE CALENDAR GRID CAN SHOW TOPIC TITLES. LAST IN THE SLICE. /meetings carries no topic ids - MeetingSummary has scheduledStart and itemCount and nothing about which topics are on the agenda; AgendaItem.topicId and topicTitle live only on MeetingDetail behind /meetings/{key}. ⛔⛔ DO NOT SOLVE THIS BY FANNING useMeetingDetail ACROSS THE VISIBLE MONTH. That is the N+1 shape and DEF-104 is this project's record of what unbounded read patterns cost; each detail response also carries attendance, discussions and the recording, so it is a heavy payload fetched for two string fields. The row names the answer: a projection on the Meetings side returning {meetingId, scheduledStart, items:[{topicId, topicKey, topicTitle}]}. That is a BACKEND change, which is why this is a slice item rather than a frontend batch. ⚠⚠ IT ADVANCES NO REQUIREMENT AND OWES NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION AGAINST FR-035 - DEC-094 d7 ruled this a refinement BEYOND a satisfied requirement, not an unmet clause. FR-035 stays Implemented: its purpose clause is 'see how topics are spread across upcoming meetings', which the per-meeting count meets, and AC-145 stated the titles-in-grid exclusion explicitly rather than quietly covering less than its criterion. ⚠ Reopening FR-035 was offered and DECLINED, as was creating a separate requirement. ⚠ The design's day cells hold two or three chips before they overflow, so verify the rendering against the reference before assuming titles are an improvement.

⚠⚠ **RIDER ADDED BY `DEC-105` d2, 2026-09-01 - A ONE-LINE COMMENT CORRECTION TRAVELS WITH THIS ITEM'S PR.** `src/Acmp.Api/Endpoints/MeetingsEndpoints.cs:51` reads *"Playback: mint a short-lived presigned MinIO URL for an uploaded recording **(any committee member)**."* **The code no longer admits any committee member.** `DEF-094`'s fix narrowed `GetRecordingUrlQuery.AllowedRoles` to `{ Chairman, Secretary, Auditor }` and added an audit emission - but **the comment that documented the wrong intent survived its own fix**, and `DEF-094` had cited that very comment as evidence of the divergence. Correct it to name the three roles.

⛔ **WHY IT RIDES THIS PR RATHER THAN GETTING ITS OWN, and why it is recorded HERE rather than only in the decision:** `DEC-073`'s attribution rule is one change, one cause, and a comment correction is small enough not to obscure attribution - the operator agreed. **It is written onto this row so it cannot be lost if this item is re-planned, deferred or re-scoped**, which is precisely the failure `DEC-102` d1 produced when a promised in-place correction lived only in a decision and was never applied. ⚠ **A comment asserting wider access than the code grants, on a sensitive-data path, is the same class that produced `DW-091`'s misreading and blocked `WBS-26.4`** - the second stale-comment instance in one session, and the first cost a build.

⚠ **IF THIS ITEM IS NOT BUILT, THE RIDER STILL OWES A HOME** - move it to whichever PR next touches `MeetingsEndpoints.cs`, or give it its own. It must not lapse with the item.

⛔⛔ **DELTA APPLIED BY `SC-044` UNDER `DEC-108` d1, 2026-09-01, BEFORE ANY CODE — THE HEADLINE ABOVE SAYS *TOPIC TITLES* AND THE DELIVERABLE IS NOW THE TOPIC **KEY**.** The pre-build sweep read `ACMP Backlog & Topic.dc.html` and found it draws day-cell chips labelled with entity KEYS, extracted programmatically from its own `calEvents` literal rather than read by eye: `TOP-009` (day 4), `TOP-018` (9), `TOP-014` (12), `MTG-019` (18), `ACT-040` (20), `TOP-009` (24). `INV-014` makes a matching `.dc.html` the visual source of truth, and **nothing in the package had ever ruled on the chip's label** — *titles* was `DW-086`'s own drafting, carried into this title unchanged when the row was scheduled. A key also fits the 10.5 px chip that a full title does not. ⚠ **The heading is left as it was written rather than rewritten, because a correction is only legible beside the instruction it replaces** — the same treatment `WBS-26.4` gave `DW-091`'s withdrawn premise. **Build the key; the word *titles* above is superseded, not current.**

⚠ **WHAT THE RULING DID NOT CHANGE, so this delta is not read as wider than it is.** The **backend projection is untouched** — `{meetingId, scheduledStart, items:[{topicId, topicKey, topicTitle}]}` already carries the key AND the title, so the contract serves either rendering and no endpoint shape moves; the operator was told so when the question was put. **v1 does not grow in WORK** — the item was already activated and scheduled by `DEC-094`/`SC-038`. **No acceptance criterion is created** and `FR-035` stays `Implemented` (`DEC-094` d7). **`AC-145` is not touched and cannot be** — it is `Met`, Approved and immutable, and its exclusion clause anticipated this residual in writing.

⛔ **BOUNDED DELIBERATELY BY `DEC-108` d2 AND d5, SO A ONE-WORD ANSWER COULD NOT SILENTLY EXPAND THIS.** The reference's calendar is a MIXED-ENTITY month view and two of its six chips are `kind:'due'` (`ACT-040`, and a second `TOP-009`). **Due and action markers stay EXCLUDED** — topics carry no due date at all (`FR-036`/`DW-001`, deferred), so building them would fabricate data, which is `SEC-537` D1's *honest empty* judgement. **The `/meetings` sibling calendar is NOT in scope** (`MeetingsCalendar.tsx`, `.mt-cal-grid`, its own reference `ACMP Meetings.dc.html`): `DW-086`'s would-serve-both clause is an ACTIVATION TRIGGER, not a statement of scope, and reading a trigger as scope is how an item silently doubles.

⚠⚠ **A CONSTRAINT THIS ROW NEVER CARRIED AND THE SWEEP FOUND: EVERY NEW INTERACTIVE CHIP MUST CLEAR A 24 px `target-size` BOX.** `ADR-0045` floored `.cal-event` at `min-block-size: 24px` on 2026-09-01 because it measured ~21 px and axe reported `serious` on every chip (`DEF-126`). ⛔ **`ADR-0045` d3 is deliberately NARROW** — it licenses the minimum change reaching AA conformance and **explicitly nothing else**, so any further departure from the reference still needs its own record. ⭐ **And the axe sweep is no longer vacuous**: it passed over an EMPTY calendar for weeks because the e2e seed sat one day outside the rendered month, and it will now catch a regression (`LL-041`).

⚠ **WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, because an unmeasured claim is counted here whether or not it comes out right.** The reference populates six cells with exactly ONE chip each, so it DRAWS one chip per cell. **That is not evidence against this row's own estimate that a cell holds two or three before overflowing**: six sparse mock entries speak to the mock's DATA, while the estimate is geometry — cell height divided by chip height. Different quantities, and the mock cannot adjudicate the second. **Only the LABEL finding is claimed.**

✅✅ **THE CELL LAYOUT IS RULED — `DEC-109` d3, 2026-09-01: THE MEETING CHIP STAYS AND THE TOPIC CHIPS NEST BENEATH IT.** `DEC-108` d1 settled the chip's LABEL; it did not settle the CELL, and the operator was asked separately rather than the layout being resolved silently. **`AC-145` is `Met`, Approved and immutable** — the store refuses to edit an approved AC at all, including to mark it superseded (`DEF-111`) — and its *Then* clause requires the meeting chip carrying the meeting title and its topic count, so **removing that chip would falsify a `Met` criterion that could never afterwards be corrected.** Nesting satisfies it while delivering what `DW-086` actually asks for: topic keys visible WITHOUT selecting a meeting.
⚠⚠ **THIS IS A RECORDED `INV-014` DIVERGENCE AND `DEC-109` d3 IS ITS RECORD, AS `ADR-0045` d3 REQUIRES.** The justification is that **the reference cannot be reproduced from this data model**: it draws one chip per cell because it assumes topics carry their own dates — a topic chip on day 4, a meeting chip on day 18. **ACMP topics have no date of their own.** `Topic.Schedule` raises an event with zero consumers and persists no meeting id, so a topic's only date is the meeting whose agenda carries it, and a topic chip therefore lands on the SAME day as its meeting chip. One-chip-per-cell is not available at any effort.
⚠ **THE LAYOUT IS RULED; THE RENDERING IS NOT ACCEPTED.** JSDOM does not render, so this gets LOOKED AT in both locales over real seeded data before anything is claimed — this project found a `.sub-card` collapsing to 43 px in RTL and a panel off-screen in both directions by looking and by nothing else. **If the cell visibly cannot hold both models, that goes back to the operator** rather than being resolved silently in either direction.

⛔⛔ **A SECURITY CONSTRAINT NEITHER THIS ROW NOR `DW-086` CARRIED, FOUND BY READING THE HANDLER THIS PROJECTION WOULD IMITATE (`PE-760`). THE PROJECTION MUST REDACT RESTRICTED TOPICS.** `GetMeetingDetail` resolves `var hidden = (await _confidentiality.GetHiddenTopicIdsAsync(ct)).ToHashSet()` and passes it into `MeetingMapping.ToDto(agenda, hidden)`; its own comment states the stakes in one sentence — *"AgendaItem froze the topic's key and title at build time, so without this the meeting hands a Restricted topic's title to the whole committee."* ⚠ **IT IS SHARPER HERE THAN ON THE PATH IT COPIES**: that path is ONE meeting reached by selecting it, while this is a BULK read over every meeting in the visible month, rendered on load with no selection, for every principal who opens the backlog calendar. An unredacted projection would broadcast a month of Restricted keys and titles to the whole committee on page load — the *second authorization path over content scoped to somebody else* shape `WBS-24.8` names as having produced `DEF-052` and `DEF-056`.
⚠⚠ **AND THE SAME COMMENT CARRIES THE PERFORMANCE HALF, WHICH APPLIES ONE LEVEL UP HERE**: *"RESOLVED ONCE PER MEETING, NEVER PER ITEM — one cross-module call for the whole agenda. Asking per item would be an N+1 over every meeting the committee ever opens."* This projection spans MANY meetings, so **resolve the hidden set ONCE for the whole month** — never per meeting and never per item, or `DEF-104`'s N+1 returns through the back door of the very fix that exists to avoid it.
⚠ **MIRROR THE AUTHORIZATION, DO NOT INVENT IT.** `GetMeetingDetailQuery` declares `AllowedRoles = Array.Empty<string>()` deliberately, per its `FR-163`/`AC-114` comment, because it is *the only read-all path that projects an agenda* and a plain Member opens it, while every other `MeetingMapping` agenda caller is Chairman/Secretary-gated. **Match the existing `GET /meetings` authorization and be no wider**, and do not enter the guest path allowlist. Its guest-scope check also answers identically whether a meeting is out of scope or absent — *"One answer for both leaves nothing to probe"* — and that reasoning transfers to any month-range query a guest could reach.
⭐ **HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method is the transferable part:** a grep for `Restricted`/`Confidentiality` across `src/Modules/Meetings/` returned **only compiled DLLs under `bin/`**, zero source files — which reads exactly like *the Meetings module does no redaction* and would have been a confident wrong answer in the dangerous direction. The redaction is real and enters through an injected abstraction whose call site names neither term. **Reading the handler is what found it** (`LL-043`).

✅✅✅ **DONE-CLAIMED 2026-09-02 — `Approved` → `Review`, BECAUSE `main` IS GREEN AND `DEC-110` d6's HOLD IS THEREFORE LIFTED.** The item itself merged as PR `#338` → `f91bf705` on 2026-09-01 and was held at `Approved` ever since, not because anything was wrong with it but because that merge-commit's CI run `33547719532` went red on `DEF-109` — d6's rule is *no item is done-claimed on a red tree, however green its own suites were*. **`main` went green at `52d89a73`** (merge-commit runs CI `33568749035` and Security `33568749019`, both success), so the condition d6 named is met on its own terms. ⚠ **`DW-086` MOVES TO `Done` IN THIS SAME BATCH** — d6 says *both move together when `main` goes green*, and a `DW-` row left `Activated` after its item ships is an omission this register has recorded FOUR times.
⚠ **`Review` IS DONE-CLAIMED, NOT VERIFIED.** `Implemented` is the operator's verdict, adjudicated per item against a generated slate (`node scripts/gen-slice-review-slate.mjs <slice id>`), never a summary (`LL-011`, `DEC-079` d3). The per-item mechanism has discriminated twice and is not ceremony.
⚠ **WHAT GREENED `main` WAS NOT THIS ITEM AND MUST NOT BE READ AS VINDICATING IT**: it was PR `#339`, `DEC-112` d2's crash-artefact instrument for `DEF-121`, which `DEC-112` d3 named as the vehicle precisely because no other code change was in flight. `DEF-109` remains `Open` at `medium` and diagnosed but unfixed, so the tree can redden again on the same fault at any time.

SL-036 - the DEF-109 capture instrument, then DW-096's host sharing. Parent of WBS-27.1 and WBS-27.2. Its own transition is a mechanical roll-up over its children and is NOT a verdict on the slice; the slice's Implemented is the operator's alone.

DEC-120 d3 - AN INSTRUMENT THAT CAN PRODUCE A `DEF-109` ARTEFACT AT ALL. FIRST IN THE SLICE, AND THE ITEM WHOSE PR GREENS THE TRUNK.

THE FINDING, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. `DEF-109`'s end condition (`DEC-110` d3) carries clause (2) - *it fires again and a captured artefact (a hang stack, a process dump, a runner resource metric) identifies a cause*. **No such artefact has ever existed for ANY of its four occurrences, and none can.** `DEC-112` d2's capture hooks `ContainerNotRunningException`, which is `DEF-121`/`DEF-130`'s container-crash path; `DEF-109`'s signature is `TaskCanceledException` at the 100-second `HttpClient` ceiling INSIDE `Acmp.Api.Tests`' own process, where no container dies and nothing is copied out. `PE-810` named this. **A clause that cannot fire is indistinguishable from the outside from a clause that has not yet fired**, and quiet time reads as progress in both cases - which is the concern `DEC-103` d1 wrote end conditions to prevent, arriving in a new costume.

SO IT IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM, NOT AN EXTENSION OF THE CONTAINER CAPTURE, AND MUST BE SCOPED AS ONE. The subject is an in-process stall in a test host, not a dead container. `docker cp` has no role.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE THE ITEM, STATED AS A CAPABILITY RATHER THAN AN IMPLEMENTATION, BECAUSE THE SIZING SWEEP COMES FIRST. When `Acmp.Api.Tests` exceeds its ~3-minute baseline or a request approaches the 100-second ceiling, the run must leave behind evidence a later reader can attribute a CAUSE from - at minimum managed thread/task state at the moment of the stall, and runner resource figures taken then rather than after. It must be attributable to the run by id, and it must survive the job.

CONSTRAINTS ANY ATTEMPT INHERITS. It must not itself perturb the thing it measures - an instrument that changes the timing of a timing-sensitive stall reports on its own presence. It must be silent and near-free on the ~99% of runs that are green, since it sits in the backend job on every push and PR. And `LL-013` binds before any of it is believed: **prove the instrument fires by injecting a fault and watching it produce output**, because a capture that has never demonstrably fired is `DEF-078`'s green control with no subject.

WHAT IT MAY NOT CLAIM. It does not fix `DEF-109` and is not a remedy for it; it makes the row's clause (2) reachable. `LL-035` governs anything that follows.

AND THE PRE-BUILD SWEEP IS MANDATORY BEFORE ANY CODE (SL-035's habit, which resized or stopped every item it was run on): sweep `requirements`, `adrs`, `decisions`, `open_questions`, `scope_changes`, `deferred_work`, `defects` AND `progress_entries` for existing coverage of test-host diagnostics, and choose the control from the register most likely to be MISSED (`LL-053`).

✅ **DONE-CLAIMED 2026-09-03, ON A GREEN TREE.** Shipped as `#342` → `d506b908`, `#343` → `01fc4eb1` and `#344` → `f5b87068`; held at `Approved` by `DEC-110` d6 through three red merge-commit runs, and released when `main` went green at `d6cd4a66` — **CI `33787859037` AND Security `33787858808`, both workflows on the same sha** (`DEC-123` d2 ruled a cancelled gating scan red, so both had to pass). No `DW-` row to close in the same batch: `trace_query` returns ZERO edges, because `DEC-120` d3 commissioned this item directly rather than activating a deferred-work row.
⭐⭐ **IT DISCHARGED ITS CAPABILITY AND ITS OWN CONSTRAINT CAUGHT ITS SUCCESSOR.** `DEF-109` occurrence 6 left the first artefact the defect has ever had (`PE-829`) and it refuted thread-pool starvation on 204 samples. ⛔ **But the trigger recorded nothing, and could not have** — the fault leaves scheduling drift at its healthy value. That is `DEF-134`, fixed in `#353` → `d6cd4a66`, and it is exactly this row's own `LL-013` clause paying: the instrument was proved to fire, and an occurrence proved the fault does not move what it fires on (`LL-055`). ⚠ **The operator's verdict on this item is theirs alone**; `Review` is done-claimed, not `Implemented`.

`DW-096` - SHARE `WebApplicationFactory` HOSTS ACROSS `Acmp.Api.Tests` INSTEAD OF BUILDING ~293 OF THEM. SECOND IN THE SLICE, DELIBERATELY, BECAUSE ITS DANGEROUS FAILURE MODE IS A PASS.

⚠⚠ ACTIVATED BY `DEC-120` d2 **OVER THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION TO CARRY**, on the `DEC-071` d3 precedent - the reasoning-against is preserved in that decision so the activation is not later mistaken for agreement about HOW. Read `DEC-120` d2, `DEC-115` d3 and `DEC-116` d4 before sizing anything. The trigger that fired is `DW-096`'s own (b), *a FOURTH `DEF-109` occurrence*, which landed 2026-09-02 (PR `#341` head `dba8d483`, CI run `33660158581`).

⛔⛔ WHAT THIS ITEM MAY NOT CLAIM, AND IT IS THE ROW'S OWN OPERATIVE CLAUSE RATHER THAN A CAVEAT (`DEC-115` d3). **It does not demonstrably remove `DEF-109`.** `PE-785`'s correction measured the hosted runner at ~16 GB, not 7 GB, which destroyed the causal bridge from *this suite retains 2.0-2.5 GB* to *the runner exhausts memory and the `TestServer` stalls* - that step rested entirely on the sum not fitting, and at 16 GB it fits comfortably. **The falsifiable claim any attempt is held to is the MEASURED one: RETENTION TRACKS HOST COUNT**, evidenced as retained managed bytes after a forced full collection and NEVER as working set (`LL-047`), and never as *CI went green* (`LL-035`).

WHAT IS MEASURED AND IS NOT IN DOUBT (`PE-771`). Identical work - 80 requests - retains 137 MB over twenty hosts and 8 MB over one. Twenty disposed factories held only by `WeakReference` are 20 of 20 still alive after a forced full GC. Retention is linear at 6.9-8.6 MB per host.

⛔ THE SMALL FIXES ARE ALREADY ELIMINATED - DO NOT RE-PROPOSE THEM. Releasing the fourteen EF InMemory stores at disposal works as a mechanism, was proved to execute (5 seeded rows to 0), and buys 3%. Stripping ALL of OpenTelemetry buys 33% and frees ZERO hosts. Stripping the rate limiter, whose timer the `gcroot` path names explicitly, changes nothing. The root path runs from process-global roots through an `ExecutionContext` captured during host STARTUP into `HostFactoryResolver+HostingListener`, across 505 unique roots - **so anything long-lived started while the host is built roots the host, and there is no single subscriber to remove** (`LL-048`).

⚠⚠ THE REAL COST, AND IT IS WHY THIS ITEM IS SECOND. Today EVERY test gets a private set of fourteen empty InMemory databases, and many seed and assert on global counts. **That isolation is free and accidental.** Sharing a host shares those databases, so each converted class needs its fixtures re-scoped or its assertions made independent of what its siblings wrote - `LL-032` pointed at the test suite itself, where **the dangerous outcome of getting the conversion wrong is a PASS, not a failure.** Convert incrementally and prove each converted class still fails when it should.

CONSTRAINTS ANY ATTEMPT INHERITS, FROM THE ROW. The factory MUST stay parameterless-constructible - `EndpointAuthorizationCoverageTests`, `WebexOAuthApiTests`, `WebexStatusApiTests` and `WebexWebhookApiTests` activate it through xUnit's fixture activator, and the source comment records that adding an optional constructor parameter failed 22 tests at construction time. Those four classes are also the proof the pattern works here. `WithIdentityProvider()` builds a DELIBERATELY different host (`ADR-0040` / `SC-005`) and cannot share one with the default, so it is a SECOND fixture rather than the same one.

AND THE PRE-BUILD SWEEP IS MANDATORY BEFORE ANY CODE, with `LL-053`'s boundary guard applied to it.

---

✅ **BUILT 2026-09-04 — DONE-CLAIMED, `PE-837` IS THE RECORD.** 287 host constructions across 43 files → **47 hosts** (42 `IClassFixture<AcmpWebApplicationFactory>` + 5 `IClassFixture<IdentityProviderHost>`), an **83.6% reduction** against `DEC-124` d1's predicted 83%. The count is EXACT, not estimated: xUnit creates one fixture instance per test class. Suite 4m17s → 38s locally. 445/445 forward, 445/445 reversed, `dotnet format` exit 0.
⭐⭐ **THE DESIGN FINDING: THE EXPENSIVE THING IS THE HOST, NOT THE DATABASE.** The fourteen InMemory stores were merely BUNDLED with the host, so one host per test bought isolation nobody asked for. `AcmpWebApplicationFactory.Reset()` — called from each class's constructor, which xUnit runs once per TEST — separates them, so every test still starts against empty tables while 240 hosts disappear. **Measured, not assumed: the naive share-everything version failed 72 of 445 first.**
⭐ **The control is `SharedHostOrderGuard`** (`ACMP_TEST_ORDER=reverse`), proved in three steps: a pre-conversion reversed baseline (445/445, so a later failure is attributable), its own mutation-checked positive control, and an INJECTED coupling that went green forward and red reversed. Its limit — reversal is one permutation — is stated in its own header.

✅ **IMPLEMENTED - PR `#365` → `89ea7f6c`, ten checks green, BOTH merge-commit runs verified (CI `33966762766`, Security `33966762739`).** `DW-098` - MediatR 12.4.1 → 12.5.0 ACROSS 15 PROJECTS, THE NINE TEST CALL SITES ADAPTED, AND A **CALIBRATED** GUARD THAT THE CALLER'S `CancellationToken` SURVIVES THE PIPELINE. ⛔ **NO PRODUCTION CHANGE - AND THAT IS A MEASURED CONCLUSION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT.**

⛔⛔ **READ `PE-875` BEFORE THIS ROW'S HISTORY CONFUSES YOU. AN EARLIER VERSION REQUIRED ALL FOUR PIPELINE BEHAVIOURS TO CHANGE `next()` → `next(ct)`. THAT REQUIREMENT WAS WITHDRAWN AND ITS PREMISE WAS FALSE.**

**WHAT THE VERSION BUMP ACTUALLY DOES.** `RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse>` gained a `CancellationToken` parameter **with a default value**. Measured by controlled pair: `await next()` compiles under BOTH 12.4.1 and 12.5.0; `await next(ct)` compiles ONLY under 12.5.0 (`CS1593` before). ⚠ **That fact is real. The conclusion drawn from it - that bare `next()` therefore forwards `CancellationToken.None` - was invented and is FALSE.**

✅ **MEASURED THREE WAYS ON THE REAL DI PIPELINE.** Bare `next()` with the caller's token pre-cancelled → handler threw `OperationCanceledException`, so **the handler got the CALLER'S token**. An innermost probe behaviour with a healthy token → saw the caller's exact token, never `None`. A probe forwarding a pre-cancelled token via `next(cancelled)` → handler threw, so **the parameter propagates when supplied**. MediatR falls back to the original token when the default is used, and the four behaviours in `Acmp.Shared` are **correct as written and deliberately untouched**.

**WHAT SHIPPED.** `MediatR` 12.5.0 in all 15 csproj files. Nine test call sites adapted in `Acmp.Application.Tests`. One calibrated guard. **Zero production files.**

**THE NINE SITES WERE CLASSIFIED, NOT TEMPLATED.** Seven of nine are `AuthorizationBehavior` DENIAL tests where `next` is NEVER INVOKED - the behaviour throws `ForbiddenAccessException` first - so asserting token forwarding there would be a hollow assertion, exactly what `DEC-132` d5's *"say so rather than writing a hollow assertion"* clause anticipated. They take a discard parameter and nothing more. Only `PresenterPreviewAuthorizationTests`' two ADMISSION tests actually invoke `next`, and all four sites in that file share one `Next` method group.

✅ **THE GUARD IS CALIBRATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `MembershipPipelineTests` composes the REAL pipeline through DI (`Logging → Authorization → Validation → handler`); a `TokenProbeBehavior` registered LAST is innermost and observes what the three above forwarded, with a per-test probe instance so nothing is shared (`LL-032`). **It was run against a deliberately broken chain and FAILED with `OperationCanceledException`, then passed against the real one** (`LL-013`, `LL-041`, `LL-055`).

**DEFINITION OF DONE - ALL MET.** `dotnet build acmp.sln -c Release` → 0 errors. `Acmp.Application.Tests` → **1212 passed**, being 1211 before plus the new guard; **no drop**, which this row named as a finding condition. Coverage gate green in CI. Both the PR run and both merge-commit runs read green (`LL-036`).

⚠ **THE ONGOING COST THIS WAS SCHEDULED TO STOP IS STOPPED:** every regenerated `dotnet-minor-patch` Dependabot group carried this bump and redded the build identically until it landed.

CAPTURE AND **UPLOAD** KEYCLOAK'S LOGS FROM THE `e2e` STACK ON EVERY NON-CANCELLED OUTCOME, NOT ONLY ON `failure()` - BECAUSE `DEF-129`'s SIGNAL ARRIVES ON RUNS THAT FINISH **GREEN**.

**THE GAP, MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED.** `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`'s `Stack logs on failure` step is gated `if: ${{ failure() }}`. On run `33933554121` - the run `PE-883` read to give `DEF-129` its mechanism - the guest test FAILED its first attempt and PASSED on retry, so the job concluded `success` and **that step was SKIPPED** (`repos/A-H-911/acmp/actions/jobs/101220601640`, step 13), while step 12 `Upload Playwright report` (`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`) succeeded and produced the `trace.zip` files that carried the client-side answer. ⚠ **`DEF-129`'s founding finding is that a green run carried the warning the next run cashed in** - so the runs that matter most are precisely the ones the existing capture ignores.

**TWO FURTHER DEFECTS IN THE SAME STEP, BOTH INDEPENDENT OF THE GATING.** It prints to the job log and **uploads nothing**, so the evidence expires with the log rather than sitting in an artefact; and it is `--tail 2000` across nine services, which that step's OWN comment already warns is the wrong instrument (*"you do not know how far back the failure is until you have found it"*, added after 200 lines covered 15 seconds). Then `Tear down the stack` runs `down -v` and the containers are gone.

**WHAT TO BUILD.** A step that writes `keycloak`, `keycloak-db` and `keycloak-config` logs to files with `--timestamps` and **no `--tail`**, gated `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, placed BEFORE the teardown, plus an `actions/upload-artifact` step on the same condition. ⭐ **Unconditional capture REMOVES the condition rather than reducing the probability of catching it** (`LL-035`) - and it deliberately avoids parsing the Playwright report to detect flakiness, which would add a channel CI does not otherwise have and is `LL-060`'s exact trap.

⛔⛔ **THE ACCEPTANCE BAR IS DELIVERY, NOT EXECUTION** (`LL-055`, `LL-041`, `LL-060`). *The step ran* is not the claim; *the artefact exists and is non-empty on a GREEN run* is. Print the line counts in the step so the job log itself carries the proof, and read the artefact from the PR's own e2e run before calling the item done. **A step that produces a zero-byte log is the failure mode this item exists to prevent** - `dmesg.tail.txt`, `journalctl.tail.txt` and `journalctl.sql.txt` are all ZERO BYTES in `DEF-121`'s capture artefact, which is the same instrument class shipping silent.

⚠ **`.github/**` IS NOT PATH-IGNORED**, so this goes branch → PR → green CI → squash-merge, and BOTH the PR run and the merge-commit run are read (`LL-036`).

⛔ **IT DIAGNOSES NOTHING.** `DEF-129` keeps `DEC-118` d2's ruling. An elimination is not an identification and neither is a successful capture - `DEC-115` d2 and `DEC-116` d1 both refused that reading on `DEF-121`.
